newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares end lower on political tension.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares end lower on political tension.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly lower on Monday in very thin trading as political tension between Israel and the Palestinians rose, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 1.40 percent, or 3.44 points, to 242.34 on very low all-share turnover of 72 million shekels against 136 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend. On Sunday there was no trading because of the Jewish holiday of Purim.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.40 percent lower at 250.34.

"The market was falling today but volume was very low. Peace talks are stuck and the whole peace process is in danger. It seems now that it is almost impossiable to reach an agreement with the Palesinian side," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities.

Israeli troops clashed on Monday with palestinians for the fifth straight day. Security forces remanied on high alert for more suicide bombings after an Islamic militant blew himself up at a Tel Aviv cafe on Friday, killing three Israeli women.
The bombing further marred Israel-PLO ties already strained over the construction of a Jewish nighbourhood in East Jerusalem.
"It's only normal that after such a bombing the market falls. The positive fact is that volume was very low and nobody is rushing to sell," said Ron Weisberg at I.B.I. Investment House.
"The current level is attractive and institutional investors are now on the buying side. Foreign investors are more cautious because they are more worried of the political situation," Weisberg added.

Scharia said that "despite the gloomy situation there is no panic or big sellers in the market". He said prices were still attractive and investors were sitting on the fence awaiting further developments.

Clal Israel fell 2.5 percent to 91 agorot. The Globes financial newspaper reported on Monday the company would post a symbolic loss in the fourth quarter of 1996 due to a compensation package for senior executives leaving the firm.

Israel Chemicals dropped 2.75 percent to 366 agorot although the company reported on Monday that net profit in the fourth quarter of 1996 rose to $12.6 million from a net loss of $9.6 million a year earlier.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which fell 2.0 percent to 537 on volume of 4.3 million shekels and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose 2.5 percent to 29,093 agorot on turnover of 3.3 million shekels.

Koor Industries, the third active share, fell 1.25 percent to 29,436 agorot on volume of 2.8 million shekels. A source said on Monday Koor is in talks to sell its 71.5 percent stake in Shemen Industries Ltd to an Israeli investment fund and a U.S. investor.
